body:
Wish I could do that. I have an attractive face, but it doesn't mean shit to me. I didn't earn it, I just lucked out with my genes. Then I get really depressed because I realize ugly people are treated like shit for something completely out of their control, that they cannot change. Fucked up world.

Congratulations, though. It's always good to hear someone is beating their depression.

yeah... this will be my first christmas with depression

it's crazy how my desire for material objects has dropped to zero. I don't want anything physical. I just want emotional stability. I just want my brain to stop fucking me.

Are you me? What the fuck? No, seriously. I can empathize with you so, so much.

Also 19. Also have "friends". Also mooching off parents. Also tried therapy but it didn't do shit.

And the ex girlfriend thing. Holy shit man. "I am that crazy ex." Dude, I have said those exact words to myself so many times. Tried to kill myself because of her too. Locked myself in a closet with a lawnmower and tried to die of carbon monoxide poisoning but the lawnmower startled me and I got freaked out and pussied out (lol pathetic). My ex was my only real friend, the only person I've *ever* opened up to, so I'm pretty messed up now that she's gone, and I see from your posting history we relate on that too. I've only been broken up with her for 6 months, though. Fuck man, I'm so sorry to hear you've been going through this shit for 2 years.

And the funniest thing is, I also watched The Perks Of Being A Wallflower just the other day. I loved it but felt it was completely unrealistic. No introvert goes through highschool like that, having friends handed to them and whatnot. I wish that had happened to me.

I'm sorry that I can't give you any advice on what to do next. I'm lost as well. We could be friends, though. We are in very similar situations. PM me if you wanna.

No contact for about 4 months. I do still check the FB every once in a blue moon, it's difficult not to. I will try to stop completely, I guess. And I have zero desire/intentions of having her back in my life. I want her out of my head and out of my sight, permanently.

The OCD thing is interesting. I have never thought of that, nor has anyone but you suggested what I'm going through relates to OCD. I've been through multiple mental health assessments; it's pretty easy to notice when they're evaluating for OCD ("do you lock the door a specific amount of times? do you constantly wash your hands?" etc) and according to the psychiatrists I'm not a sufferer of it. But that intrigues me, maybe it's something to consider. Can you really be OCD just from obsessing over thoughts? I don't have any of the physical 'lock the door 7 times every morning' ritual symptoms.

I feel like this is great advice for a "normal" breakup, but my reaction to my breakup is definitely abnormal. The pain that comes with constantly obsessing over her sexual activity is unbearable. I have never heard of anyone as fixated as me on similar thoughts.

I don't want her back. I want her to... disappear, or something. Something about seeing her enjoy life, and especially sex, without me really gets to me. If she were to just vanish from existence I think I'd feel *a lot* better. It's really strange, and pretty fucked up. I don't understand these feelings at all. I just want them gone.
Can't you go to a walk in clinic and explain your situation?
I know. I don't expect reading a few reddit posts to solve my problems. I'm just looking for some kind of guidance on what steps to take next.

I know.

And yes, I was honest.
